title: 2 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who was the man of Belial that blew a trumpet and declared no allegiance to David?
questions.correctAnswer: Sheba, the son of Bichri
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:1 states that the man of Belial who blew the trumpet and declared no part in David was Sheba, the son of Bichri.

questions.question: What did Sheba say after blowing the trumpet?
options: We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse
Let us unite under one king
Victory to the house of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 20:1, Sheba declared, 'We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse.'

questions.question: After Sheba's declaration, which group followed him?
questions.correctAnswer: Every man of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:2 says that every man of Israel went up after David and followed Sheba, but the men of Judah stayed with David.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Judah followed Sheba after he blew the trumpet.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:2 explains that the men of Judah clave unto their king David, not following Sheba.

questions.question: What did King David do with his ten concubines during this time?
options: Put them in ward and fed them but did not go in unto them
Sent them away to other cities
questions.correctAnswer: Put them in ward and fed them but did not go in unto them
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:3 states that David put the ten concubines in ward, fed them, but did not go in unto them, and they lived in widowhood until their death.

questions.question: Who did David command to assemble the men of Judah within three days?
questions.correctAnswer: Amasa
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:4 records that David said to Amasa, 'Assemble me the men of Judah within three days.'

questions.question: True or False: Amasa assembled the men of Judah exactly within the time appointed by David.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:5 says that Amasa tarried longer than the set time appointed by David.

questions.question: According to David, who would cause more harm than Absalom?
questions.correctAnswer: Sheba the son of Bichri
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:6 shows David saying Sheba the son of Bichri would do more harm than Absalom.

questions.question: Who did David instruct to pursue after Sheba?
options: Amasa with the men of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Abishai with the lord's servants
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:6 records David telling Abishai to take the lord's servants and pursue Sheba.

questions.question: Who led the men that went out of Jerusalem to pursue Sheba?
questions.correctAnswer: Joab's men
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:7 states that Joab's men, along with Cherethites and Pelethites, went out to pursue Sheba.

questions.question: Where did Amasa go before the men as they pursued Sheba?
questions.correctAnswer: The great stone in Gibeon
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:8 says that when they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa went before them.

questions.question: True or False: Joab greeted Amasa by taking him by the beard to kiss him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:9 records Joab taking Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

questions.question: What fell out of Joab's garment as he went forth?
questions.correctAnswer: A sword
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:8 mentions that a sword fastened on Joab's girdle fell out as he went forth.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 20, which instruction comes first?
options: David tells Amasa to assemble the men of Judah
Sheba blows the trumpet and declares no allegiance to David
David puts his concubines in ward
questions.correctAnswer: Sheba blows the trumpet and declares no allegiance to David
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with Sheba blowing the trumpet and making his declaration in verse 1, before the other events.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Judah clave unto their king from Jordan even to Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:2 states that the men of Judah clave unto their king from Jordan to Jerusalem.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did Joab kill in a surprise attack while pretending to greet him?
questions.correctAnswer: Amasa
questions.explanation: Joab killed Amasa by smiting him in the fifth rib during a feigned greeting, as described in 2 Samuel 20:10. This is the only incident where Joab kills this person in the chapter.

questions.question: What was the immediate effect on the people after Amasa was killed and removed from the highway?
options: They all went on after Joab to pursue Sheba
questions.correctAnswer: They all went on after Joab to pursue Sheba
questions.explanation: After Amasa was removed from the highway, all the people continued after Joab to pursue Sheba, showing their loyalty and desire to quell the rebellion, as in 2 Samuel 20:12-13.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 20, what was the wise woman's role in resolving the siege at Abel of Bethmaachah?
options: She negotiated peace by offering tribute
She convinced the city to surrender Sheba's head
She led the city's defense against Joab
She called for reinforcements from David
questions.correctAnswer: She convinced the city to surrender Sheba's head
questions.explanation: The wise woman spoke to Joab and arranged for the people to cut off Sheba's head and throw it to Joab, effectively ending the siege (2 Samuel 20:16-22).

questions.question: How does the wise woman describe the people of Abel in her plea to Joab?
options: As peaceable and faithful in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: As peaceable and faithful in Israel
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 20:19, the wise woman identifies herself and her people as peaceable and faithful, appealing to Joab not to destroy their city.

questions.question: What reason did Joab give for besieging the city and pursuing Sheba?
options: Sheba had lifted his hand against the king
Sheba was a priest who rebelled
questions.correctAnswer: Sheba had lifted his hand against the king
questions.explanation: Joab explained to the wise woman that Sheba, a man of mount Ephraim, had rebelled against King David, justifying the siege (2 Samuel 20:21).

questions.question: What action did Joab take immediately after receiving Sheba's head?
options: He blew a trumpet and withdrew
He sent a messenger to David
questions.correctAnswer: He blew a trumpet and withdrew
questions.explanation: After the wise woman arranged Sheba's death, Joab blew a trumpet signaling the end of the siege and the troops retired to their tents (2 Samuel 20:22).

questions.question: Who was placed over the tribute in David's administration according to this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Adoram
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:24 states that Adoram was over the tribute in King David's administration.

questions.question: What does the death of Amasa teach about trust and vigilance in leadership conflicts?
options: That trusting appearances can be dangerous
That mercy is always the best policy
questions.correctAnswer: That trusting appearances can be dangerous
questions.explanation: Amasa was killed unexpectedly when he did not notice Joab's sword during a greeting (2 Samuel 20:9-10). This warns about being vigilant and cautious in leadership disputes.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 20, the people of Judah abandoned David to follow Sheba the son of Bichri.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states the men of Israel followed Sheba, but the men of Judah cleaved to their king David from Jordan to Jerusalem, showing their loyalty.

questions.question: True or False: Joab was appointed over all the host of Israel as stated at the end of the chapter.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:23 confirms Joab's position as commander over all the host of Israel.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 20:11-13 imply will happen if Amasa is removed from the way and Joab leads the pursuit?
options: The people will stop following Joab
The people will continue pursuing Sheba with Joab
questions.correctAnswer: The people will continue pursuing Sheba with Joab
questions.explanation: Verse 11 encourages those favoring Joab to follow him, and verses 12-13 show that after removing Amasa's body, the people resumed pursuit under Joab's leadership.

questions.question: How does the chapter illustrate the virtue of wisdom through the actions of the wise woman in Abel?
options: By using force to defend the city
By negotiating peace and saving the city
By fleeing to warn King David
questions.correctAnswer: By negotiating peace and saving the city
questions.explanation: The wise woman used wise counsel and negotiation to end the siege without destruction, demonstrating wisdom in conflict resolution (2 Samuel 20:16-22).

questions.question: What does the chapter suggest about obedience to rightful authority in the context of Sheba's rebellion?
options: Rebellion against the king is justified
Loyalty to the king is vital to Israel's stability
Ignoring the king leads to prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Loyalty to the king is vital to Israel's stability
questions.explanation: Sheba's rebellion caused division and war, while the men of Judah remained loyal to David, highlighting the importance of obedience to legitimate authority (2 Samuel 20:1-2).

questions.question: What role did Abishai play after Amasa's death according to the chapter?
options: He accompanied Joab in pursuing Sheba
He led the siege in Abel alone
He was left in Jerusalem to guard the king
questions.correctAnswer: He accompanied Joab in pursuing Sheba
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:10 states that after killing Amasa, Joab and Abishai pursued Sheba together.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter shows that even close family members can be involved in violent conflicts during times of rebellion.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joab killed Amasa, who was his relative (brother), illustrating that family ties did not prevent deadly conflict in this rebellion (2 Samuel 20:8-10).

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 20.

questions.question: What reason does the wise woman give for urging Joab not to destroy the city of Abel?
options: Because the city was under David's direct protection
Because the city was peaceable and faithful in Israel and part of the LORD's inheritance
Because Sheba was hidden inside the city
Because the city had strong fortifications
questions.correctAnswer: Because the city was peaceable and faithful in Israel and part of the LORD's inheritance
questions.explanation: The wise woman states she is peaceable and faithful in Israel and questions why Joab would destroy a city that is the inheritance of the LORD, as found in 2 Samuel 20:19.

questions.question: How does Joab respond to the wise woman's plea about destroying the city?
options: He agrees to spare the city unconditionally
He denies any intention to destroy the city or swallow up the inheritance of the LORD
He threatens to destroy the city regardless
questions.correctAnswer: He denies any intention to destroy the city or swallow up the inheritance of the LORD
questions.explanation: Joab replies emphatically that it is far from him to destroy or swallow up the city, as seen in 2 Samuel 20:20.

questions.question: Who is identified as the instigator against King David, according to Joab's explanation to the wise woman?
options: Sheba the son of Bichri from mount Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: Sheba the son of Bichri from mount Ephraim
questions.explanation: Joab explains that Sheba the son of Bichri, a man of mount Ephraim, lifted his hand against King David, as stated in 2 Samuel 20:21.

questions.question: What action did the people of Abel take after the wise woman's counsel regarding Sheba?
options: They surrendered Sheba alive to Joab
They cut off Sheba's head and threw it over the wall to Joab
They hid Sheba in secret tunnels
They fortified the city to resist Joab
questions.correctAnswer: They cut off Sheba's head and threw it over the wall to Joab
questions.explanation: Following the wise woman's advice, the people beheaded Sheba and cast his head to Joab over the wall, as described in 2 Samuel 20:22.

questions.question: Which two groups were commanded by Benaiah, according to the chapter's final verses?
options: The mighty men and the scribes
questions.correctAnswer: The Cherethites and the Pelethites
questions.explanation: The text states Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites in 2 Samuel 20:23.

questions.question: What position did Adoram hold during David's reign as mentioned in this chapter?
options: Over all the host of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Over the tribute
questions.explanation: Adoram was appointed over the tribute, as recorded in 2 Samuel 20:24.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the wise woman’s speech which references a historical proverb about Abel, effectively resolving the conflict?
questions.correctAnswer: Allusion
questions.explanation: The wise woman alludes to an old saying that counsel was always sought at Abel, invoking historical wisdom to resolve the siege (2 Samuel 20:18-19). This is an example of allusion.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'man of Belial' in reference to Sheba signify in the context of this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: A worthless or wicked person
questions.explanation: The term 'man of Belial' (2 Samuel 20:1) is a Hebrew expression meaning a worthless or wicked person, indicating Sheba's character as a rebel and troublemaker.

questions.question: Which verse describes Joab’s killing of Amasa, and what might this event foreshadow in biblical narrative terms?
options: 2 Samuel 20:10; foreshadows violent power struggles in David's kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 20:10; foreshadows violent power struggles in David's kingdom
questions.explanation: Joab’s murder of Amasa in 2 Samuel 20:10 foreshadows the intense and often violent political struggles during David’s reign and his successors.

questions.question: How does the theme of loyalty to the king versus tribal allegiance appear in this chapter, particularly in verses 1 and 2?
options: Sheba’s rebellion causes the northern tribes to separate from David, while Judah remains loyal
questions.correctAnswer: Sheba’s rebellion causes the northern tribes to separate from David, while Judah remains loyal
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 2 show Sheba rallying Israel (mainly northern tribes) against David, while Judah remains loyal, highlighting tribal divisions and loyalty conflicts.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage shares a similar theme of rebellion against a king and the subsequent pursuit of the rebel, as seen in 2 Samuel 20?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Kings 1 (Adonijah's rebellion)
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1 recounts Adonijah's rebellion against Solomon, mirroring themes of royal challenge and pursuit seen in 2 Samuel 20, reflecting recurring conflict over Davidic succession.

questions.question: What is the significance of Joab blowing a trumpet after Sheba’s head is thrown to him, according to the cultural context of ancient Israel?
options: It signals the start of a festival
It announces the end of the rebellion and calls the troops to stand down
It is a call to further battle
questions.correctAnswer: It announces the end of the rebellion and calls the troops to stand down
questions.explanation: The trumpet blown by Joab (2 Samuel 20:22) signals the cessation of hostilities and orders the troops to return to their tents, indicating the rebellion’s end.

questions.question: True or False: Joab was over all the host of Israel during the events described in this chapter.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:23 explicitly states that Joab was over all the host of Israel, confirming his military leadership.

questions.question: True or False: The ten concubines taken by David were immediately sent away from the palace after Sheba’s rebellion began.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 20:3 explains that David put the ten concubines in ward and fed them but did not go in to them, keeping them shut up until their death, not sending them away.

questions.question: Who was the recorder during David's reign as mentioned in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud is named as the recorder in 2 Samuel 20:24, responsible for official record-keeping.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Sheba's declaration in 2 Samuel 20:1 reveal about human rebellion against God-appointed leadership?
options: It shows a rejection of God's anointed king and a desire for division
It expresses loyalty to David as God's chosen leader
It indicates a call for unity under David's reign
It reveals submission to the son of Jesse
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a rejection of God's anointed king and a desire for division
questions.explanation: Sheba's statement 'We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse' (2 Samuel 20:1) reveals a deliberate repudiation of God's chosen king, illustrating human sinful rebellion and the fracturing of God's people under disobedience.

questions.question: What does the loyalty of the men of Judah to King David in 2 Samuel 20:2 imply about the nature of covenantal faithfulness?
options: It demonstrates steadfast allegiance to God’s anointed despite national division
It shows political opportunism without spiritual conviction
It indicates rejection of David’s kingship
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates steadfast allegiance to God’s anointed despite national division
questions.explanation: The men of Judah cleaving unto David from Jordan to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 20:2) shows covenantal faithfulness, highlighting God’s providential preservation of His anointed king amidst rebellion, a pattern echoing divine faithfulness in Scripture.

questions.question: What theological significance can be derived from David's action toward his concubines in 2 Samuel 20:3?
options: It illustrates judgment and sanctification through separation and restraint
It shows indulgence in sinful desires
It depicts David's disregard for his household
It indicates political alliance through marriage
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates judgment and sanctification through separation and restraint
questions.explanation: David shutting up his concubines and not coming unto them (2 Samuel 20:3) symbolizes a purification process, representing sanctification and the moral consequences of sin, foreshadowing the call to holiness in God's people.

questions.question: What does the delay of Amasa in assembling the men of Judah in 2 Samuel 20:5 teach about human weakness in leadership during crises?
options: It reveals the fallibility and unreliability of human leaders
It shows divine approval of procrastination
It indicates perfect obedience to the king
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the fallibility and unreliability of human leaders
questions.explanation: Amasa's delay beyond the appointed time (2 Samuel 20:5) exemplifies human weakness and failure in leadership, emphasizing the need for God's sovereignty over human agents in fulfilling His purposes.

questions.question: How does Joab’s killing of Amasa in 2 Samuel 20:10 reflect on the tragic consequences of sin and power struggles within God’s people?
options: It portrays the destructive nature of sin and ambition even among God's servants
It demonstrates God’s endorsement of violent power grabs
It reveals divine judgment on Amasa
It shows a peaceful resolution to conflict
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays the destructive nature of sin and ambition even among God's servants
questions.explanation: Joab’s murder of Amasa (2 Samuel 20:10) reveals how sin and ambition corrupt even those close to God's purposes, causing internal strife and illustrating humanity’s fallen nature apart from God’s grace.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine justice can be inferred from the people’s reaction to Amasa’s death in 2 Samuel 20:12-13?
options: God’s justice halts the advance of violence until proper order is restored
God condones all acts of violence without question
Divine justice is irrelevant in human conflicts
The people ignored justice and proceeded without restraint
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice halts the advance of violence until proper order is restored
questions.explanation: People standing still and removing Amasa’s body from the highway (2 Samuel 20:12-13) suggests a respect for justice and order, reflecting God’s sovereign governance even amid human disorder.

questions.question: How does the siege of Abel of Bethmaachah in 2 Samuel 20:15 help us understand God’s patience in dealing with rebellion?
options: The extended siege shows God’s restraint and opportunity for repentance
It indicates immediate destruction without warning
It represents God’s abandonment of His people
It displays God’s indifference to sin
questions.correctAnswer: The extended siege shows God’s restraint and opportunity for repentance
questions.explanation: The city’s siege (2 Samuel 20:15) reflects God’s patient long-suffering, providing time for repentance before final judgment, consistent with His attribute of mercy (cf. Exodus 34:6).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the wise woman’s intervention in 2 Samuel 20:16-21?
options: God’s wisdom and providential guidance through human agents
God’s wrath and destruction without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wisdom and providential guidance through human agents
questions.explanation: The wise woman’s speech and negotiation (2 Samuel 20:16-21) reveal God’s providence and wisdom working through unexpected individuals to bring peace, underscoring His sovereign control over history.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the beheading of Sheba in 2 Samuel 20:22?
options: The doctrine of justice and the consequences of rebellion against God’s anointed
The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of divine election without human responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of justice and the consequences of rebellion against God’s anointed
questions.explanation: Sheba’s execution (2 Samuel 20:22) demonstrates divine justice manifesting through human agency, showing the serious consequences of opposing God’s established order.

questions.question: How does Joab’s role as commander in 2 Samuel 20:23-26 reflect the biblical principle of delegated authority in God’s kingdom?
options: It shows God’s ordaining of human leaders to carry out His purposes
It suggests that leadership is based solely on personal ambition
It reveals chaos without any structured leadership
It indicates that only kings have authority
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s ordaining of human leaders to carry out His purposes
questions.explanation: Joab’s command and the appointment of others (2 Samuel 20:23-26) illustrate the biblical principle that God delegates authority to human leaders to sustain His kingdom’s order and accomplish His will (Romans 13:1).

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined theological insight do 2 Samuel 20:1-2 and 20:22 teach about sin, judgment, and restoration in God's covenant community?
options: Sin leads to division and rebellion, but God’s justice brings restoration through judgment
Sin is irrelevant as God always restores without judgment
Rebellion is encouraged to test God’s patience
Judgment always results in permanent destruction with no hope
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to division and rebellion, but God’s justice brings restoration through judgment
questions.explanation: Sheba’s rebellion (2 Samuel 20:1-2) caused division, but his death (2 Samuel 20:22) restored peace, demonstrating the biblical truth that sin disrupts God’s people but divine justice ultimately restores order.

questions.question: Synthesis: How do 2 Samuel 20:3 and 20:10 together illustrate the consequences of sin on leadership and personal relationships within God’s people?
options: Sin results in broken relationships and tragic outcomes among God’s leaders
Sin has no consequences in leadership roles
God allows sin to strengthen relationships
Sin only affects outsiders, not God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: Sin results in broken relationships and tragic outcomes among God’s leaders
questions.explanation: David’s treatment of his concubines (2 Samuel 20:3) and Joab’s murder of Amasa (2 Samuel 20:10) reveal how sin damages personal and leadership relationships, underscoring the need for repentance and sanctification.

questions.question: Synthesis: What does the interaction between the wise woman and Joab in 2 Samuel 20:16-21 reveal about God’s use of wisdom and mercy to resolve conflict, in light of Joab’s military actions in 2 Samuel 20:15?
options: God combines justice and mercy, using wisdom to bring peace amid judgment
God favors only military strength without mercy
Mercy is irrelevant in conflict resolution
Wisdom always leads to more violence
questions.correctAnswer: God combines justice and mercy, using wisdom to bring peace amid judgment
questions.explanation: The siege (2 Samuel 20:15) represents God’s judgment, while the wise woman’s plea (2 Samuel 20:16-21) exemplifies God’s mercy and wisdom working to restore peace, illustrating the balance of divine justice and compassion.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 20:6 reveal the reality of spiritual warfare and the ongoing opposition to God’s kingdom?
options: Sheba’s rebellion represents an intensified attack against God’s anointed, symbolizing spiritual opposition
It shows that all opposition is merely political
It denies any spiritual dimension to conflict
It suggests God is powerless against rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: Sheba’s rebellion represents an intensified attack against God’s anointed, symbolizing spiritual opposition
questions.explanation: David’s concern that Sheba will do more harm than Absalom (2 Samuel 20:6) highlights the ongoing spiritual opposition to God’s kingdom, reflecting the biblical theme of Satanic resistance against God’s rule (Ephesians 6:12).

questions.question: Apologetics: Sceptics claim that 2 Samuel 20 portrays God as endorsing political violence and murder. What does 2 Samuel 20:9-10 actually teach about God's sovereignty and human responsibility in the context of Joab’s killing of Amasa?
options: God permits human free will within His sovereign plan, but does not endorse sin; Joab’s act shows human sinfulness, not divine approval
God directly commands all acts of violence described
The text glorifies Joab’s violence as righteous
God is absent from all human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God permits human free will within His sovereign plan, but does not endorse sin; Joab’s act shows human sinfulness, not divine approval
questions.explanation: While Joab’s murder of Amasa (2 Samuel 20:9-10) is recorded, the narrative does not justify it as godly; this illustrates human sinfulness and the complexity of divine sovereignty allowing human choices without endorsing sin (cf. Romans 8:28).
